classification.difficultyReason: Sketch restricted linear, quadratic and cubic functions, distinguishing included endpoints, excluded endpoints and discrete domains.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph of each of the following functions, and find its domain and range.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=3x+1$ only for $-1\le x\le1$. Both endpoints are included.
$$\begin{align*}f(-1)&=3(-1)+1=-2\\f(1)&=3(1)+1=4\end{align*}$$
The line increases from $(-1,-2)$ to $(1,4)$, so $\operatorname{dom}(f)=[-1,1]$ and $\operatorname{ran}(f)=[-2,4]$.

spec.description: Increasing line segment with both endpoints closed; no grid or numeric axis ticks.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=-x+1$ only for $-3\le x<2$.
$$\begin{align*}f(-3)&=-(-3)+1=4\\-2+1&=-1\end{align*}$$
The line decreases from the closed endpoint $(-3,4)$ towards the open endpoint $(2,-1)$. Thus $\operatorname{dom}(f)=[-3,2)$ and $\operatorname{ran}(f)=(-1,4]$.

spec.description: Decreasing line segment with left endpoint closed and right endpoint open.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=\dfrac{x+1}{2}$ only for $-3\le x<3$.
$$\begin{align*}f(-3)&=\frac{-3+1}{2}=-1\\\frac{3+1}{2}&=2\end{align*}$$
The line increases from the closed endpoint $(-3,-1)$ towards the open endpoint $(3,2)$. Thus $\operatorname{dom}(f)=[-3,3)$ and $\operatorname{ran}(f)=[-1,2)$.

spec.description: Increasing line segment with closed left endpoint and open right endpoint.

answer.worked: Sketch the part of $y=x-2$ with $x\ge0$. It begins at the closed endpoint $(0,-2)$ and continues upwards to the right. The least output is $-2$, and the outputs have no upper bound. Thus $\operatorname{dom}(f)=[0,\infty)$ and $\operatorname{ran}(f)=[-2,\infty)$.

spec.description: Line ray with a closed starting point and an arrow indicating continuation.

answer.worked: Sketch the part of $y=-x+2$ with $x<2$. Mark $(2,0)$ as an open endpoint and continue the line upwards to the left. Every output is positive; $0$ is not attained. Thus $\operatorname{dom}(f)=(-\infty,2)$ and $\operatorname{ran}(f)=(0,\infty)$.

spec.description: Line ray continuing upwards to the left from an excluded endpoint.

answer.worked: Sketch the downward-opening parabola $y=-x^2$ only for $-2<x<2$. Its vertex $(0,0)$ is included. The endpoints $(-2,-4)$ and $(2,-4)$ are open, so the output $-4$ is excluded. Thus $\operatorname{dom}(f)=(-2,2)$ and $\operatorname{ran}(f)=(-4,0]$.

spec.description: Downward parabola with both boundary points open and its vertex included.

answer.worked: Sketch the right-hand branch of $y=(x-1)^2$, beginning at the closed vertex $(1,0)$. Its least output is $0$, and it increases without bound. Thus $\operatorname{dom}(f)=[1,\infty)$ and $\operatorname{ran}(f)=[0,\infty)$.

spec.description: Right-hand parabola branch, closed at its vertex; bounded display window represents an unbounded curve.

answer.worked: Sketch the left-hand branch of $y=-(x+2)^2$, excluding its vertex $(-2,0)$. All outputs are negative and decrease without bound as the curve continues to the left. Thus $\operatorname{dom}(f)=(-\infty,-2)$ and $\operatorname{ran}(f)=(-\infty,0)$.

spec.description: Left-hand downward parabola branch with its vertex excluded.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=x^3$ only for $-1\le x\le1$.
$$\begin{align*}f(-1)&=(-1)^3=-1\\f(0)&=0\\f(1)&=1\end{align*}$$
The curve increases between the closed endpoints $(-1,-1)$ and $(1,1)$. Thus $\operatorname{dom}(f)=[-1,1]$ and $\operatorname{ran}(f)=[-1,1]$.

spec.description: Increasing cubic segment with both endpoints included.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=-x^3$ only for $-1\le x<1$.
$$\begin{align*}f(-1)&=-(-1)^3=1\\f(0)&=0\\-(1)^3&=-1\end{align*}$$
The curve decreases from the closed endpoint $(-1,1)$ towards the open endpoint $(1,-1)$. Thus $\operatorname{dom}(f)=[-1,1)$ and $\operatorname{ran}(f)=(-1,1]$.

spec.description: Decreasing cubic segment with closed left endpoint and open right endpoint.

inlines.text: The vertex is included; the endpoint giving 4 is excluded.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=(x-1)^2\\f(1)&=0\\f(2)&=1\end{align*}$$
Sketch the parabola only for $-1<x\le2$. Its vertex $(1,0)$ is included, $(-1,4)$ is open and $(2,1)$ is closed. The minimum output is $0$. The output approaches $4$ but never reaches it on this domain. Thus $\operatorname{dom}(f)=(-1,2]$ and $\operatorname{ran}(f)=[0,4)$.

spec.description: Restricted parabola with open left endpoint, included vertex and closed right endpoint.

answer.worked:

Plot only $(0,3)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$ and $(3,0)$; do not join them because the domain contains only four inputs. Thus $\operatorname{dom}(f)=\{0,1,2,3\}$ and $\operatorname{ran}(f)=\{0,1,2,3\}$.

spec.description: Four isolated closed points; no joining lines.

answer.worked:

Plot only $(-2,4)$, $(-1,1)$, $(0,0)$, $(1,1)$ and $(2,4)$; do not join them. Repeated outputs are listed once in the range. Thus $\operatorname{dom}(f)=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$ and $\operatorname{ran}(f)=\{0,1,4\}$.
